speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Here, I would like to state for the record, deep appreciation for the work done by our Multi-Ministry task force and our frontline workers.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Their dedication, courage and sacrifices in fighting the COVID-19 outbreak is admirable and will always be held in gratitude by all of us.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: The COVID-19 outbreak has disrupted our lives on many levels.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Our personal freedom has been curtailed and our livelihoods have suffered a beating.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Some of us have had to change the way we work – whether it is working from home, doing flexi-work, working in split teams, or working extended shifts on the frontlines.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: A vast majority of Singaporeans understand the need for these changes and restrictions.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: We understand that in order to reduce and eventually eradicate the COVID-19 infections, we need to restrict movement and interactions as much as possible, even though these restrictions will impact livelihoods.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: For some of us, we are not sure if work will still be there for us or if we are able to continue to provide for our families – when we go on sick leave, when we are asked to go on no-pay leave or worse, when we are retrenched or lose our only source of income.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: For those among us who are retrenched or have had their source of income cut off, home-based businesses (HBBs) such as baking or cooking, or selling crafts or other items from home, allow them to earn a living despite the current COVID-19 circuit breaker (CB) measures in place.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: For these HBBs, their choices are very limited, and they are the ones we worry about.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: They need time to make adjustments, especially where their income is concerned.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: For the affected HBBs, they did not just suffer a loss of income, they also saw their own hard-earned savings put to waste.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: It is not an easy life for HBBs.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: I know because I grew up as the daughter of a home baker.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: My mother used to sell pineapple tarts, peanut cookies and lapis cakes when I was growing up.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: She used to get only two or three hours of sleep so that she could fulfil her orders, which were aplenty during festive seasons.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: This was on top of her day job as a typist.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: I helped to put the little floral dough on top of the pineapple filling of the tarts and the little peanut pieces on the cookies, and I was the one to help her butter the baking sheets onto the baking tins.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: But it helped to supplement our family income especially when my late father lost his job for a period of time.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: But then again, I was probably one of the lucky ones.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: My mother still had a day job and some income, and the home baking was to supplement what she earned.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: For some among us, it is not quite the case.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Her husband lost his job as a driver because of his diabetes and heart condition.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Her mother-in-law, who lives with her, is advanced in age, of poor health and unemployed.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: So, she bakes from home and sells them.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Her Nutella tarts and brownies are to die for.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: I have ordered from her and there was once when I offered to give some extra cash to help the family.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Her sense of dignity in wanting to earn through her own toil and sweat and creativity, is admirable.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: She does not want handouts and she takes pride that she is able to put food on the table and pay for her family's expenses through her own hard work and creativity.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: She is dignified and empowered, knowing that the best help is in her hands.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Take also the example of Ms Sery, who is a home baker and single mother of five school-going children.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Some may lament and say that she should work as there are childcare or after-school care arrangements for her children.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: But Ms Sery is so good at baking and decorating cakes, and like Mdm N, she is dignified and empowered, knowing she is able to use her creativity to put food on the table, and be there for her children as well.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Yet another home-based business owner is Ms Adeline Tan.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Ms Tan had to go through a couple of eye surgeries, which would have disrupted a more permanent form of employment.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: With her passion in baking, she decided to be a home baker so that she can hone her craft and have that dignity of being able to support herself through her passion and talent.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: The dignified tenacity and resilience of home bakers and home business owners such as Mdm N, Ms Sery and Ms Tan, they are admirable.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: They do not want to be a burden to society and they want to strike out on their own, on the path they all know well.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Just like when we had to become self-reliant when we gained independence as a nation.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: In addition, may I ask why introduce the blanket ban on 25 April in the first place, which was then back-pedalled on 2 May, when the announcement to ease restrictions was made – a matter of only one week?

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Did HBBs pose a serious COVID-19 related risk in the first place that required a blanket ban?

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: The blanket ban imposed severe disruptions and inconveniences to many HBBs.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: As I mentioned earlier, orders have had to be cancelled or put on hold, refunds have had to be made, and to some extent, raw ingredients already purchased have had to be discarded.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: For the HBBs that were affected, they did not just suffer a loss of income, they also saw their own hard-earned savings put to waste.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Here, I wish to put forth a few suggestions for the Government to consider implementing, should restricted measures still need to be in place.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Hence, contactless collection and delivery can be arranged and carried out.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: This was what the HBBs were asking for when the ban was introduced.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Going forward, the third-party delivery companies can even be assigned ones for HBBs to use, so that there is close monitoring of who the delivery personnel are.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: This will facilitate contact tracing efforts, if required.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Two, those HBBs who are already under HDB's Small-scale Business Scheme will continue to adhere to current food hygiene rules, if they are doing baking or cooking businesses.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: If, and only if, there is any worry or concern about their health during this COVID-19 circuit breaker period, these HBB owners can be asked to log their temperature checks and health declaration daily.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: This can be done through a mobile application that can be easily set up.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: This will give assurance to consumers and the authorities that the HBBs are generally in good health and do not pose any COVID-19 related risks.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: In this way, hygiene, health and temperature checks, and centralised and monitored deliveries, can all be done more easily.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: This is a good initiative but we also recognise that not all HBBs can work in central kitchens or work away from home.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: But at least, this can be an option for some HBBs to continue operations during the period of restricted measures.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: However, this would also mean increased costs for those who run the central kitchens.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: The suggestions above are in no way asking for special waivers of current CB measures.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: All along, HBBs have not asked for special treatment, exceptions or waivers of any of the current CB measures.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: At this juncture, Mr Speaker, please allow me to speak in Malay.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: (In Malay):   I am particularly concerned about the fate of home-based businesses (HBBs) because I myself grew up as a child whose mother had a home-based business.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: At one time, my mother sold pineapple tarts, peanut cookies and lapis cakes to supplement our family’s living expenses, and the additional income from the sale of her cookies really came in handy when my late father lost his job temporarily.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: My mother, who comes from our Merdeka generation, was an independent person who always displayed perseverance.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Just like the rest of our Merdeka generation, our HBBs also displayed an unwavering spirit.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: This spirit must be encouraged because it is the same spirit that propelled us to develop Singapore after we achieved independence.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: This is also the spirit emulated by our HBB owners like Mdm N.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: She supports her husband who lost his job as a driver because of diabetes and heart condition, and their son is studying in Primary school.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: I have ordered Nutella Tarts and brownies on several occasions from Mdm N.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: I have also offered to give her some extra cash to help her with her expenses.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: She said she can still earn a living through her own toil and sweat.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: She does not simply hope for handouts and she wants to earn her own income to pay for her family's expenses and living.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Our HBB owners are not asking for exemptions from the current restrictions or regulations.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: They are just asking for an equal opportunity to continue their businesses, just like retailers who are allowed to use third-party delivery services, for instance.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: I shall not repeat the suggestions that I mentioned earlier.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: I hope the authorities can consider these suggestions seriously.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Once again, I would like to emphasise that none of these suggestions are asking for any exemptions from the restrictions or regulations that must be implemented for the sake of public health and safety.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: (In English): In conclusion, Mr Speaker, I wish to reiterate that our HBBs are not asking for special treatment or waivers of current CB measures in place.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: All they are asking for is equal treatment, clarity and consistency and an opportunity to carry on their businesses, while still observing restrictions that are in place.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: I hope that in doing this Adjournment Motion and speaking for our HBBs, we are able to demonstrate empathy, understanding and leadership in finding ways to reconcile our differences and arrive at inclusive solutions for our HBBs, while still complying with the restrictions that need to be in place, in the interest of public health and safety.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: It is the kind of leadership that people need in times of difficulty.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: After all, if they are like us, then their struggles are our own.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: If we fail to help, we diminish ourselves.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: And another by Audrey Hepburn, and I quote, "Nothing is more important than empathy for another human being's suffering.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: We have to feel for one another if we are going to survive with dignity." That is all from me.

speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: I welcome the announcement made on Saturday on the easing off some restrictions to some businesses, including home-based business (HBB) which will be allowed to operate with some restrictions from 12 May onwards.

speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: There are also many types of home-based business (HBB) owners.

speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Some do it full-time and others may be seasonal and carry out their business during festive seasons.

speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: However, the impact of COVID-19 on home-based business (HBB) during the circuit breaker period varies, with some facing financial distress even with the lifting of restrictions.

speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Another problem home-based business (HBB) is the inability to fulfil the orders leading to customers asking for refunds.

speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: The orders are usually small amounting to less than few hundred dollars but when combined can amount a few thousand dollars.

speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: The deposit paid by customers may have been used to purchase materials needed to fulfil the orders.

speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: They will incur a loss if their customers insist on a refund instead of postponing the orders.

speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Neither is seeking a legal recourse a practical option as legal fees are expensive.

speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: The best way forward is to negotiate with the counter party and try to arrange in such a way that they can postpone delivery.

speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Here, I would like to make a call to HBB owners and customers, to be gracious and come to an amicable settlement, especially during this difficult time.

speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Failing which, the HBB owner might lose a customer permanently and get bad reviews on social media and a customer that would just have to suck it up.

speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: (In Malay):   During this COVID-19 crisis, there are Home-Based Businesses or HBBs that may encounter financial hardship even though several restrictions will be eased.

speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Most HBBs do not have a "Scheduled Contract" and will not be able to avail themselves to the reliefs under the COVID-19 (Temporary Measures) Act 2020.

speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Here, I would like to call on the HBB owners and customers to negotiate amicably in order to reach a settlement that will not burden any party.

speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: (In English): I would like to end my speech by thanking our President Halimah Yaacob on her Facebook post where she connected well and showed great empathy toward the home-based business (HBB) owners.

speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: I would also like to thank Mr Lawrence Wong and our Ministers in the Inter-Ministerial Task Force for their leadership in steering Singapore through this crisis.

speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: I believe great leadership is not only about making the hard decisions but, having empathy and the ability to relate to and connect with the people that are hardest hit to gain their trust and providing the support needed to cushion the impact on their lives.

speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Without a doubt, our Ministers have demonstrated great leadership.

speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: And to the thousands of frontline workers, your display of courage and tenacity is undeniable and we are immeasurably grateful to all of you.

speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: I hope, once this crisis is over, as a society, we will accord the due recognition for the important work of essential workers by ensuring fair wages and benefits are accorded to them.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: It is hard speaking just after taking out the mask.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: I too salute Mdm N, Ms Sery and Ms Tan for their spirit of self-reliance.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: I too can empathise with Dr Intan's mother who supplemented her income with a home-based business.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: This was what many Malay families and many of us in the Chamber have gone through.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: My mother, too, operated a home-based business when my father passed on.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: So, when I empathise deeply with their challenges, I say this as someone who lived that life.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Many housewives juggle, taking care of their children and elderly parents, and running these businesses to supplement their incomes.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: The tightening of circuit breaker measures has put restrictions on many businesses, including HBBs.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: For HBBs catering to the Malay/Muslim community, I understand their disappointment, especially those who had been gearing up for Ramadan and Hari Raya celebrations.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: But the COVID-19 crisis is not about preserving livelihoods alone.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: The crisis has forced many governments, many of us, to make stark choices between preserving livelihood and preserving life itself.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Indeed, their plight reflects the difficulties many Singaporeans currently face.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Many have lost their jobs or have been placed on no-pay leave, so through no decisions of this Government.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: And even for those of us who still have our jobs, we are confined to our homes, going out only for essentials and exercise.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: But I believe many support the circuit breaker and agree that it is necessary.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Before this, we routinely had more than 50 new cases daily.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Like many countries, the risk of cases growing exponentially was real and this is the reason why it is hard to plan and prepare our citizens for what comes next.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: We had to act fast and hard to minimise people movement and social interactions.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: We understand this has been painful for everyone.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Non-online HBBs could normally run without oversight or registration as they were typically small and do not disturb their neighbours.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: However, their informal and dispersed nature presents a special challenge during COVID-19.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: We cannot enforce safe distancing in them the same way we do for commercial orders.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: This poses a real risk when people move and interact in residential estates, as goods are collected and delivered.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: It takes just one infected person to start a cluster.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Lives, especially of our elderly, are at stake, and they can be right in the homes of this HBB operations.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: The circuit breaker would need to be extended if community transmissions remained high.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: We are just making a decision because the situation has improved.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Hence, as we made the difficult decision to restrict the operations of HBBs.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Because everyone, including the HBBs, complied with the measures, we are seeing earlier results.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: We are therefore gradually relaxing restrictions from 12 May.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Beyond allowing retail sale of cakes and confectionery for takeaway and delivery, we are resuming food HBBs for delivery and collection only.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: But we are not out of the woods yet, because clusters can still form as activities and interactions increase.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Food HBBs, their customers and delivery personnel have to comply with a set of safe distancing measures – practising contactless delivery and collection, and installing TraceTogether to help contact tracing.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Dr Intan suggested channelling HBBs is to central kitchens, but this is not necessary with the latest position and may result in even greater movement of people.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Other non-online HBBs are to remain closed for now.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Food HBBs can now accept and start preparing orders to be fulfilled after 12 May.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: It is hoped – as I had expressed in my Facebook post – that you will be in time for Hari Raya Puasa, even if we must be prepared for a quieter Raya.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Just to preserve lives, we know we still have to take care of those directly affected by the COVID-19 situation and those affected by decisions to curb is exponential growth in infection.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: MOF has introduced schemes over three Budgets to support our businesses, workers and those in need.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: All Singaporeans aged 21 and above also received a once-off Cash and Support payout in April.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Many HBB operators would have benefited from the Temporary Relief Fund that was meant for relief in April.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: From May, as Mr Zainal inquired, self-employed HBB owners can apply for the Self-Employed Person Income Relief Scheme, or SIRS, or the COVID-19 Support Grant if they do not qualify for SIRS but are salaried employees who lost their jobs, suffered pay cuts or were placed on involuntary no-pay leave.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: SSOs will also extend other forms of support like ComCare for low-income families who need help.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Many members of the Malay/Muslim community have stepped up to calm worries and extended help to food HBBs.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: This is the correct spirit in the holy month of Ramadan.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: For instance, the Singapore Malay Chamber of Commerce and Industry (SMCCI) quickly got in touch with over 1,800 HBBs.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: SMCCI helped qualify HBBs so that they could access the Temporary Relief Fund automatically.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: They are advising them on how to tap on other Government support schemes.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: SMCCI is also looking to provide capability and capacity building for HBBs.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: If there is a silver lining, the HBBs now have SMCCI to champion and help them run viable and resilient micro-businesses.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: I also thank lawyers in the M3 community who, together with SMCCI, extended free legal advice to HBBs concerned about the legal implications of failing to fulfil their obligations, like issues around deposits and inability to deliver in time.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: (In Malay):   I am deeply concerned and sympathise with those from our community who depend on their home-based businesses as a source of income.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Those who have accepted orders during the months of Ramadan and Syawal will be most affected, especially since orders during Ramadan may have dipped slightly this year due to COVID-19.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: However, we need to minimise all movement and interactions so that we do not spread the virus to the elderly, to our families and to our friends.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Some adjustments have to be made, just like how some of us have adapted to a very different Ramadan this year.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: This will give the business owners some time before Hari Raya Aidilfitri, even as this year’s celebrations will require some adjustments as well.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: The situation has improved, not by chance, but because we stayed home and observed safe distancing.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: But we must not be complacent – we are dealing with a cunning virus and a difficult adversity.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: If we have reaped anything from this, it was to give focus to food HBBs to do your part to enforce safe distancing during food preparation.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: I also hope that through the crisis, they will be reborn resilient, like Dr Intan's mother.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: For those HBBs that remain suspended, please be patient.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Restrictions can only be lifted gradually and carefully when the situation continues to improve.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: We must prevent infections from spreading uncontrollably because when that happens, nature will take a tragic course.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: The more united we are in observing the circuit breaker, the sooner we can lift the measures.
